title: 1. Archive audit: slow-attractor escape versus tail intermittency
hypothesis: Learned re-capture preferentially rescues persistent-slow episodes rather than suppressing intermittent tail failures.

prediction.against: R-116 module on the same archived R-118 confirmation cases
prediction.rationale:
Measure persistent-slow completed-failure prevalence across all 1,536 cases; a five-percentage-point reduction would locate a substantial part of CONTINUE's gain without spending simulator episodes.

FROZEN DEFINITIONS (triage round 1; only the totals of non-successes and drops are known so far, no split has been computed). Data: the r116 and continue cells of logs/pen_spin/r118_recovery_retry/confirmation (twelve manifests, 1,536 cases each, paired by case); the retry, r106 and reference cells are tabulated beside them. Labels per episode, exhaustive and exclusive: success (sustained); drop (not completed; early if its length is below 60 steps, late otherwise); off_centre (completed, not sustained, final centre distance >= 0.08 m); persistent_slow (completed, not sustained, centred, final-second hit fraction <= 0.2); intermittent (completed, not sustained, centred, hit fraction strictly between 0.2 and 0.8); near_miss (completed, not sustained, centred, hit fraction >= 0.8). Registered statistic (failure_labels): the paired difference, R-116 minus CONTINUE, of the persistent_slow indicator over the 1,536 cases, with a two-sided 95% paired t interval and a manifest-clustered interval (t over twelve manifest means): supported if the paired lower bound >= 0.05, refuted if the upper bound < 0.05, otherwise inconclusive. Reported, not registered: the full label table for all five policies, the R-116 -> CONTINUE transition table, the same paired differences for intermittent, near_miss and drop, and for CONTINUE's remaining failures the mean final-second |axial rate|. Zero simulator episodes, zero LLM calls; no new seed.

falsified_by: The upper 95% confidence bound on R-116-minus-CONTINUE persistent-slow prevalence is below 0.05; an interval including zero is inconclusive about a reduction.

approval.note: I accept the implementer's now-applied label definitions, registered statistic and diagnostic tables: they make this archive-only audit executable for zero simulator episodes and zero LLM calls. Reusing the existing Stage-3 script and config is appropriate. Its limitation is interpretive: final-seco

result.notes: Archive only (R-118's twelve confirmation manifests, five policies paired by case); definitions frozen in the record before any split was computed. The whole ladder, persistent-slow episodes of 1,536: reference 699, R-106 root 568, R-116 module 333, CONTINUE 194 (RETRY 191). Of R-116's 333 persistent-slow cases, 127 become CONTINUE successes, 163 stay persistent slow, 12 become late drops. CONTINUE's remaining 395 non-successes: 194 persistent slow (mean final-second rate 1.9 rad/s), 58 intermittent (6.3 rad/s) and 39 near misses (7.0 rad/s), i.e. 97 episodes that roll fast but miss the every-step rule, 46 early drops (identical cases in every trained policy: the capture transient before step 60, untouched by anything so far), 26 late drops (during or after re-capture), 32 off-centre. Intermittent and near-miss failures also fell slightly (-0.010 and -0.009), so continued training did not trade persistent-slow rescues for unsteady rolls.

verdicts.reasoning: The paired R-116-minus-CONTINUE difference in the persistent-slow indicator is +0.090 with a 95% interval [+0.073, +0.108] over 1,536 shared cases (333 vs 194), manifest-clustered [+0.079, +0.102]; the lower bound is above the registered 0.05. Continued training's gain is located almost entirely in rescuing persistent-slow episodes (127 of them become successes); intermittent and near-miss failures did not rise.
verdicts.next_experiment: CONTINUE's remaining failures: 194 persistent slow (12.6%), 97 fast-but-unsteady (intermittent or near miss, 6.3%), 46 early drops (3.0%, the same cases for every trained policy), 26 late drops, 32 off-centre. Run R-121 (joint adaptation with matched boundary controls) next; the early drops are a separate lever (the capture transient before step 60) that nothing has addressed.

verdicts.reasoning: Persistent-slow failures decreased from 333 under R-116 to 194 under CONTINUE across 1,536 paired cases, a failure_labels reduction of 0.09049 [logs/pen_spin/r120_tail_audit/summary.json]. The paired 95% interval is [0.07296, 0.10803], placing its lower bound above the registered 0.05 threshold [logs/pen_spin/r120_tail_audit/summary.json]. The manifest-clustered interval, [0.07920, 0.10179], also clears that threshold [logs/pen_spin/r120_tail_audit/summary.json]. This supports the registered prevalence prediction, but outcome-label transitions alone do not establish a causal slow-attractor escape mechanism [logs/pen_spin/r120_tail_audit/summary.json].

direction: Continue Stage-3 Shadow Hand axial rolling by testing reward-trained symbolic residuals and incremental policy construction. Use the frozen D-072-qualified controller as the experimental reference, without changing the saved default incumbent. First compare independent parameter draws, ARS/CEM and PPO on one identical sparse, state-conditioned symbolic residual family. If an inner learner produces a confirmed useful gain, compare fixed structure, grammar-based structural evolution and LLM-guided structural evolution with that learner and inherited parameters. Investigate compact memory or anchored component replacement only when the preceding results motivate them. Preserve the task, frozen evaluation manifests and strict paired promotion/drop criteria. Run one protocol at a time. No controller-generation LLM calls during P1; advisor calls for the research loop remain allowed. Later controller-generation calls need an agreed protocol and explicit call budget. Do not repeat R-102, retune its confirmation cases, reopen cold whole-controller generation, or resume expert cloning. Continue evidence-driven follow-ups within this direction through the existing loop, including its escalation and exhaustion rules.

advisor.reasoning: This archive-only audit offers useful failure localization for zero simulator episodes and zero LLM calls, using the existing Stage-3 script and config. Its weakest point is that zero tail hits identifies a tail outcome rather than proving persistent slowness throughout the episode; the protocol appropriately limits attribution to description. The predicted failure_labels decrease of at least 0.05 versus archived R-116 is refuted if the upper 95% bound on R-116-minus-CONTINUE persistent-slow prevalence is below 0.05.

implementer.reasoning: Free and worth three minutes, but the record does not define 'persistent slow', the statistic or its interval. Proposed: exhaustive labels (success; drop early/late at step 60; off-centre; persistent slow = completed, centred, final-second hit fraction <= 0.2; intermittent = between 0.2 and 0.8; near miss >= 0.8), the registered statistic = the paired R-116-minus-CONTINUE difference of the persistent-slow indicator over the 1,536 shared cases with a paired t interval and a manifest-clustered one, and the transition table and other label contrasts as diagnostics. No split has been computed yet; only the non-success and drop totals are known.

advisor.reasoning: I accept the implementer's now-applied label definitions, registered statistic and diagnostic tables: they make this archive-only audit executable for zero simulator episodes and zero LLM calls. Reusing the existing Stage-3 script and config is appropriate. Its limitation is interpretive: final-second slowness describes a tail outcome, not persistent slowness throughout an episode or a causal rescue mechanism. The predicted failure_labels decrease of at least 0.05 versus archived R-116 is falsified if the upper 95% paired bound on R-116-minus-CONTINUE persistent-slow prevalence is below 0.05.

implementer.reasoning: Approve: labels, the registered paired statistic, its two intervals and the diagnostics are frozen before any split is computed; zero simulator episodes.
